clue.text: Maybe bow's shot showing expertise in Sherwood?

parts.note: the bow of a ship is its fore part; 'maybe' flags an example
the 's taken as written
to have a shot is to make a try

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's archery skill on display in Sherwood Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' looks like the archer's weapon, but here it is the front of a boat. Sherwood is the forest of Robin Hood legend, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Forestry is the science and craft of managing woodland, the kind of know-how a forest like Sherwood needs.

clue.text: Iron clothes in the morning for dance show

indicators.note: used as a verb, to clothe is to dress or wrap something up inside

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a.m. denotes the morning

explanation.surface: Someone doing the ironing in the morning before going to a dance performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron clothes' reads as household chores; 'clothes' is a verb meaning dresses or wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame is the stage musical and TV series set in a New York performing arts school, centred on dancing.

clue.text: Mark on uniform damaged in riot

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is to behave in a wild, uncontrolled way, which is what being in riot describes.

clue.text: Manage at home with lovely nurse coming round

parts.note: super means excellent or lovely
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Coping at home with the help of a charming visiting nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last words join and wrap around the short word for being at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To superintend is to oversee and direct, a formal synonym for manage.

clue.text: Scotsman had to bag trash in cleric's office

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a sack, so one part holds another

parts.note: Rab is a typical Scottish man's name, short for Robert
to bin something is to trash it
had a meal, so ate

explanation.surface: A Scotsman was made to bag up rubbish in a churchman's office.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scotsman and 'had' join, then hold the word for trash between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbinate is the position or term of office of a rabbi, a Jewish religious teacher.

clue.text: Chat about head of finance in taxi

indicators.note: riding in a vehicle means sitting inside it, so the other parts go within

on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of finance

explanation.surface: Talking about the finance director while riding in a cab.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab, short for confabulation, is an informal conversation or chat.

clue.text: Fellow's outer door starts to open after knock

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first of each is used

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A college fellow's front door, which opens when someone knocks.
explanation.walkthrough: In Oxford and Cambridge colleges the heavy outer door of a set of rooms is called the oak; closing it is 'sporting the oak'.
explanation.definitionFit: At old universities the solid external door to a don's rooms is traditionally named after the wood it is made from.

clue.text: Fast asleep after lying down

definitions.meaning: second meaning: lying prone and dead to the world

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast asleep' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits after the first word into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both going at maximum speed and being horizontal and completely exhausted or sleeping.

clue.text: Notice sticker up in office electioneer vacated, supporting Clinton

indicators.note: in a down entry, something supporting another holds it up from underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: Bill Clinton, the former US president
holding a post means being in office

parts.note: the word emptied of its middle leaves its outside letters

explanation.surface: A campaign poster about a politician's office, put up to back Clinton.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'supporting' means placed beneath, so the president's first name goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A billposter is a person paid to paste advertisements and notices on walls and hoardings.

clue.text: Retail event that's small beer

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A shop promotion dismissed as trivial, 'small beer' being something unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small beer' is an idiom for something trivial, but here the two words are read separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale is a period when a shop offers goods at reduced prices, a classic retail event.

clue.text: Pressure on football club to get some balls

indicators.note: in an across entry, placing one thing on another means adding it after

parts.note: Man U is the common short name for Manchester United
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A football club under pressure needs to buy more footballs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' looks like footballs, but the definition is slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: To man up is to find the courage to face a difficulty, which is what getting some balls means in slang.

clue.text: Bar's last pot to clear up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to exclude someone, as from a club by secret vote
second meaning: in pool, the final ball potted to clear the table

explanation.surface: Clearing up the last glasses at a pub at closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' and 'pot' suggest a pub; in pool the eight ball is sunk last to finish the frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to vote to exclude someone from membership and the final ball in pool.

clue.text: Cheers at the Olympics intensified

parts.note: surface reading: a stadium crowd roaring ever louder
setter's reading: 'cheers' meaning thanks, said with emphasis in the language of the 2024 Paris Games

explanation.surface: The crowd noise at the Games grows louder and louder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is the British informal thank-you; the 2024 Olympics were in Paris, so the thanks are French, strengthened with the French for 'very much'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means thank you very much, an emphatic version of the casual thanks 'cheers'.

clue.text: OK, what might a flea-ridden bear get in winter?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: satisfactory, of an acceptable standard

definitions.text: what might a flea-ridden bear get in winter?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a hibernating bear rousing itself to deal with an itch

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a whimsical literal reading: bears sleep through winter, so an itchy one would have to wake briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means meeting the required standard, which is what OK means.

clue.text: Expensive stuff in the window at GAP sells badly

indicators.note: done badly suggests things are botched and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Pricey items in a Gap shop window fail to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expensive stuff in the window' looks like displayed merchandise; it is the window pane itself. Gap is a clothing chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Plate glass is thick, high-quality sheet glass used for large shop windows, costly compared with ordinary glass.

clue.text: Compare Liz with Boris's predecessor — we mustn't have her back

indicators.note: refusing her back means her rear end is cut off, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
Ken Livingstone was Mayor of London before Boris Johnson

explanation.surface: A political jibe comparing Liz Truss with Boris Johnson's forerunner and refusing her return.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz Truss followed Boris Johnson as Prime Minister, so 'predecessor' tempts towards Theresa May; it is his predecessor as London mayor. 'Her back' is Liz's final letter, which goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them or point out their similarity.

clue.text: New tea set Pip wants

indicators.note: something new is made fresh, so the letters are formed into a different arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Pip, perhaps the boy from Great Expectations, would like a new tea set.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetites are desires or cravings, so the noun 'wants' is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Favourite uncle manipulated with a childish impatience

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: manipulated means handled and moved about, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A favourite uncle gets manipulated by a child's impatient whining.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is sulky, bad-tempered irritability of the sort associated with a sulking child.

clue.text: American's hat trick putting European record in danger

indicators.note: putting one thing in another means placing it inside, working together with the following word
in completes the instruction to place the first parts within the last

parts.note: a threat is a danger
E is the abbreviation for European
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A sportsman's hat trick threatens to break a European record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hat trick' reads as a cricket or football feat; the definition asks for the American term for three straight championships.
explanation.definitionFit: In US sports slang a three-peat is winning a title three times in a row, the equivalent of a hat trick.

clue.text: Oven one opens touching hot potato

indicators.note: something that opens a thing splits it apart and sits in the gap

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
an oast is a kiln for drying hops
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tricky issue, a hot potato, that touches on someone opening the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot potato' looks like the idiom for a controversial issue, but it is literal: a potato fresh from roasting. Roastie is British slang for a roast potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A roastie is a roast potato, served hot from the oven with a Sunday dinner.

clue.text: Several crosses mark battlefield

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it from one side to the other, enclosing it

parts.note: some means several
M is the abbreviation for the old German currency, the mark

explanation.surface: Rows of crosses marking the graves on a war battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crosses mark' paints war graves; 'crosses' means spans or straddles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is the French river and region where one of the bloodiest battles of the First World War took place.

clue.text: Labour in 2024? A lot are switching

parts.note: many means a lot

indicators.note: switching means swapping places around, so these letters change order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Many voters switched to the Labour Party in the 2024 general election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' suggests the British political party, which won the 2024 election; here it means work, measured over a year such as 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-year is a unit measuring the amount of work one person does in a year, so labour spread across a calendar year.

clue.text: Issue of one's own, when phoney Dr Chandler Bing releases book

indicators.note: something phoney is fake and made up, so the letters are reworked
to release something is to let it go, so that part is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.walkthrough: Chandler Bing is a character from the sitcom Friends. Bing loses its B before the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandchildren are the offspring of one's own offspring, issue being a formal word for children.

clue.text: Rwandan who also must be heard

indicators.note: being heard means spoken out for the ear, so the sound rather than spelling counts

parts.note: also means too

explanation.surface: A Rwandan who also demands to have their voice heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are the majority ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi, so a member is a Rwandan.

clue.text: Unknown priest going to heaven, incredibly

explanation.surface: An obscure priest unbelievably ends up in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, rising upwards towards heaven turns the priest's title upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Incredibly can be an intensifier meaning extremely, which is what this adverb means.

clue.text: Aunt short of time keeps mislabelled fruit machine

being short of something means lacking it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
botanically a fruit, though usually called a vegetable

explanation.surface: An aunt short of time keeps a fruit machine with the wrong labels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit machine' looks like a slot machine, but they split: 'mislabelled fruit' is the tomato and 'machine' alone is the definition. The aunt loses her T.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating machine, especially one that imitates a person or animal.

clue.text: Online supervisor sulks, removing 50% of content

parts.note: someone who sulks is in a mood

explanation.walkthrough: The inside of the word for a sulk is a double letter; dropping half of that leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mod, short for moderator, polices an online forum or chat group.

clue.text: Don't worry about her elephant hides

clue.text: Meter made by Siemens went round

clue.text: Reluctance to move grey hat fixed on lady's head

parts.note: the first letter of lady
